text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementTechnologyA Process Made for Mars is Now Uncovering Ancient Art on EarthAnd you can even run it on your own phoneDNBy David Nield11:30 AM CDT on September 15, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWhat do cavemen and NASA researchers have in common? Both of their work benefits from the decorrelation stretch technique—a method of image processing originally developed by NASA scientists to tease out details of satellite imagery, including photos of Mars. Now, though, it’s also being used to reveal hidden cave art here on Earth.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 OTD in Space – August 4: Phoenix Mars Lander LaunchedShareNextStayWhile the intricacies of the process are complex, it reveals details that are difficult to see to the naked eye by remapping the colors of a picture across a greater range of shades. A faint red and a slightly darker red can suddenly become a bright red and a bright green, depending on the information in the image. Basically, it’s a high-powered contrast enhancer.Read more: “The Best Mars Photos Taken by the Curiosity Rover”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
